entries.title: Travel time to a kind of place, not just an address
entries.text:
Travel time could answer "how long to my office". It could not answer "how long to a supermarket".

Now it can. In Settings, Travel time, add a place type: pick a category (supermarket, bakery, pharmacy, doctor, nursery, school, gym, park, restaurant, post office), say how you get there, and every listing is measured to the nearest one Fredy can find. The places come from OpenStreetMap.

From there it behaves like any saved address. The time shows on cards, in the table, on the map, in notifications and on the listing page, which also names the place it found. A job can put a limit on it in the same Travel time limit section as everything else.

Your existing addresses are untouched.

entries.title: The routing dials moved into the interface
entries.text:
How hard Fredy leans on Transitous and Overpass used to live in the database only. There is now an Admin, Travel time page for it: both endpoints, how many listings a sweep works through, how long answers are kept, and a switch for place lookups.

Saving an address now also says what it queued, and the Travel time page shows how far the sweep has got. Measuring is deliberately a trickle, so a few hundred listings take a few hours, and now you can watch it rather than wonder.

entries.title: Fredy can leave Germany
entries.text:
For its whole life Fredy could only find an address in one country: countrycodes=de was baked into the geocoder, and the map was fenced to the German border. Anyone turning up with a Swiss or French portal hit a wall that had nothing to do with their provider.

A provider can now say where it works. One optional line - countries: ['fr'] - and the geocoder searches there, the map opens there, and you can draw a search area there. Several countries at once are fine, and Fredy asks for them in a single request.

Nothing changes for the provider shipping today. Leave the line out and it means Germany, exactly as it always did.

So if you have been sitting on a provider for your country: now is the moment. CONTRIBUTING.md shows how.

entries.title: Tell a job how far you are willing to travel
entries.text:
Fredy already knew how long it takes to get from your saved addresses to every listing. Now a job can act on it.

In the job form, set how long the trip to each place may take. Leave a place empty and that search does not check it. Then pick what happens to a listing over the limit: only mark it on the map, keep it but send no notification, or filter it out completely.

Listings are coloured against that limit on the map and on their cards: green inside it, amber slightly over, red too far. Each one is graded by the job that found it, so the colours stay right with every job on screen.

Nothing is ever held back on a travel time Fredy could not work out.

entries.title: Set up a notification once, use it everywhere
entries.text:
Until now, every job carried its own copy of your Telegram token. Ten jobs meant ten copies, and rotating that token meant editing all ten.

A saved configuration is now called a notification channel, and it lives in one place: Settings → Notification channels. Set one up there, then pick it in as many jobs as you like. Edit it once and every job follows.

Your existing setups have been moved over for you, so nothing needs doing. A few things that were awkward before now just work: a job can hold two channels of the same kind (family chat and work chat, both on Telegram), you can duplicate a channel instead of filling the whole form again, and deleting one is blocked while a job still uses it, so a search can never quietly stop notifying you.

Admins can also share a channel with everyone on the instance. Sharing lets other people send through it, it never shows them the credentials.

entries.title: Routing got even better
entries.text:
In this release, I gave routing and travel time some more love.
  • Real travel times on every listing
  • A "reachable within" filter
  • The real route drawn on the (details)map
  • Settings → Addresses is now Settings → Travel time

Fpr more information, see the github release notes.

entries.title: Quality of life improvements
entries.text:
This release is all about quality of life improvements.
  • Map view improvements
  • ÖPNV popover behavior configurable (opens either on click or hover)
  • Settings are now more accessible, split between user and admin-settings
  • If price tracker is enabled, you can now start it manually

entries.title: Fredy watches the price
entries.text: A flat that has been on the market a while often gets cheaper, and until now there was no way to notice. Fredy can re-check the listings it has already found and record what they cost each time, so every listing carries its own price history and you hear about it when one drops. It is off by default: every check costs a page load at the portal, so switching it on is a decision you make deliberately. You will find it under Administration → Execution, together with the dials for how often Fredy looks and how many listings it touches per run.

entries.title: Fredy goes ÖPNV
entries.text: Finding a flat is one thing. Getting out of it every morning is another. Fredy now knows how well connected every listing is. Within the map view, you now have an ÖPNV layer which is enabled by default. This layer shows you the nearest bus/tram stop including the live data of which type of transportation leaves at a specific time :)
